scenes.title: The Offers
scenes.text: After months of applications and a lot of waiting, the offers come in. Some come through job boards. Some come through people: a professor, a former boss, a friend's parent. Who {name} knows shapes which doors open, and the pay behind them.
scenes.authorFlag: Referral odds are placeholders; oi_college_admissions and oi_social_capital support the direction, not the size.

scenes.title: A First Real Job
scenes.text:
{name} has to decide what to do with the offers, and with the next few years. A job that pays more might mean moving somewhere expensive. A job closer to home might pay less but come with dinner at {poss} parents' place on Sundays.

Some of {poss} friends are taking the first thing that pays. Others are holding out for something better, which is easier when someone else is covering the rent.

choices.label: {Subj} goes to graduate school
choices.description: Two more years of school, and more debt, for a higher ceiling.
choices.authorFlag: Graduate school cost and stipends are not in the data yet.

choices.label: {Subj} moves home to save money and keeps looking

scenes.title: Age {age}
scenes.text: Another year goes by: rent, work, calls home, a friend's wedding. Here's how the money looks.

researchNote.title: Behind the Story: Twenty-Five
researchNote.text: Young full-time workers with a bachelor's degree earn a median of {stat:recent_grad_median_wage} a year, compared with {stat:recent_hs_median_wage} for those with only a high school diploma. The gap is real, but so is the debt, and the degree has to be finished to pay off.
